item.title: Trump signs Russia sanctions bill into law, allowing up to 100% tariffs on India
item.description: President Trump has officially enacted a new sanctions law aimed at Russia and Iran, empowering the U.S. to impose penalties on nations purchasing Russian energy supplies. Countries like India and China, significant buyers of Russian crude and gas, have raised concerns about the potential impact on India-US relations and energy security. Both Russia and China have also expressed their discontent towards these sanctions.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: US reaches deal with Denmark for ‘permanent security control’ over Greenland
item.description: The United States and Denmark are in the final stages of discussions to enhance US military operations in Greenland. This strategic arrangement will not infringe on Greenland's autonomy, affirming its status as a Danish territory. The talks also involve strategies to curb Chinese activity in this vital Arctic locale. A potential agreement might include establishing a US missile defense system, with an official update expected shortly.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: Meet Dina McCormick, whom Zuckerberg asked to trade her Meta board seat for a job
item.description: Born in Cairo, Egypt and raised in Texas, Dina Powell McCormick gave up her Meta board seat last December after Mark Zuckerberg asked her to take an operating job instead. Nine months on, the Goldman Sachs veteran and former deputy national security adviser is president, vice chairman and co-leader of Meta Compute, handling the company's hardest legal, political and financial problems as its 2026 AI capex guidance climbs to as much as $145 billion.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Trump bans news outlets CNN, MS NOW, Politico from White House
item.description: President Donald Trump has enacted a swift exclusion of three major news outlets—CNN, MS NOW, and Politico—from White House premises. He branded their regular reports as 'FAKE NEWS,' marking a bold stance against media he perceives as adversarial. Trump warned that more outlets could follow if they continue to publish misleading narratives about his presidency.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: Mamata moves Supreme Court against EC decision to freeze TMC name, symbol
item.description: Mamata Banerjee has challenged the Election Commission's decision in the Supreme Court. The poll panel froze the Trinamool Congress name and symbol for upcoming bypolls. Her faction received a new name and symbol for the October 6 elections. The rival faction was allotted a different name and symbol by the ECI. The dispute over the original party identity remains unresolved by the commission.
item.dc:creator: AYUSH PANDEY

item.title: RBI has record forex reserves, but why is rupee still not out of the woods?
item.description: The currency is now hovering back to its two-month lows. While the RBI is intervening to prevent major volatility, the fact is the rupee is still facing immense pressure, and experts believe the currency is unlikely to appreciate much any time soon.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: Asian Games: Karate team leaves without coaches; equestrian riders caught in accred maze
item.description: For the karate contingent, reigning Asian champion Alisha Choudhary’s repeated pleas to sports authorities and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) officials for accreditation for her coach, Vikas Panchal, have gone unheard.
item.dc:creator: SABI HUSSAIN

item.title: New Orleans turns 12 million pounds of glass into sand to rebuild wetlands
item.description: In a groundbreaking initiative in New Orleans, discarded glass bottles are being turned into sand for coastal restoration. Known as Glass Half Full, this program has successfully redirected millions of pounds of glass from local landfills. Current research is examining the positive impact of this recycled glass sand on the growth and durability of wetland vegetation, providing a creative solution to Louisiana's ongoing coastal land loss issues.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Detectorists found 2,584 silver pennies; hoard later valued at £4.3 million
item.description: Recently, a noteworthy trove of Norman-era silver coins was obtained for the nation, worth £4.3 million, establishing it as the most significant treasure discovery in British history. This cache highlights the political turmoil that ensued post-Norman Conquest of England. Thanks to funding from the National Lottery Heritage Fund, this historic treasure will be displayed nationwide and will eventually find its way back to Somerset.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Google cofounder Larry Page’s wife’s company has donated over $120m in ocean projects
item.description: Lucinda Southworth, married to Google co-founder Larry Page, is a passionate advocate for ocean conservation through her organization, Oceankind. Since 2018, Oceankind has generously contributed over $120 million to improve marine ecosystems and support community health. With a focus on addressing pressing challenges like climate change and pollution, the organization champions innovative solutions and effective policies to protect our oceans worldwide.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Why too much kindness can feel uncomfortable, according to psychology
item.description: Receiving kindness can be an uncomfortable experience for many, invoking feelings of awkwardness. This unease can originate from various psychological factors and past experiences. Some view kindness as an obligation or believe they must earn affection. Likewise, receiving compliments can conflict with one's self-perception. Cultivating the ability to accept little gestures of care can significantly reduce this discomfort.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: From Macaca to MAGA: How one needling remark can become a political thorn for Trump
item.description: A 2006 incident involving Senator George Allen and a racial slur highlights how small remarks can alter election outcomes. Recent social media posts by Republican Bo French have also drawn significant criticism and condemnation. These events suggest a growing unease among some Republicans regarding Trump's influence. Moderate Republicans and even prominent figures are distancing themselves from controversial rhetoric. Such shifts could impact the upcoming midterm elections and future political landscapes.
item.dc:creator: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA

item.title: Simone Biles’ $3M mansion: How did she build her Texas lakefront estate?
item.description: Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens’ Texas lakefront mansion is finally complete after years of planning, approvals and construction delays. The couple started designing the home in 2020 and finished it in November 2025. The reported $3 million property includes a private gym, pool, sports court, large kitchen, spa-style bathroom, laundry room and a dedicated space for their dogs.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Sophie Cunningham’s inspiring journey: How did she rise to WNBA stardom?
item.description: Sophie Elizabeth Cunningham’s inspirational story is a tapestry of athletic versatility, family support, financial hardship and perseverance. Cunningham’s journey from Columbia, Missouri, to the WNBA and the Indiana Fever has been filled with both success and personal trials. Her college record, her professional career, her injuries, her demanding schedule, and her relationship with her fans give a broader view of an athlete whose story is much more than basketball.

item.title: UN report finds widespread sexual violence in Ukraine war, 89% of cases linked to Russia
item.description: A UN report documented widespread sexual violence by Russian forces in Ukraine. These violations included gang rape and genital mutilation against civilians and prisoners. Ukrainian authorities were responsible for a smaller number of similar human rights abuses. Most victims of sexual violence in detention were men, according to the UN findings. The report highlights the ongoing nature of these abhorrent acts amid the conflict.

item.title: Bristol’s £9.7m Harbour Walkway links Temple Meads to £500m campus
item.description: Bristol City Council spent £9.7 million on a 400-metre floating Harbour Walkway, initially estimated at £2.5 million and designed to connect Temple Meads station to a planned music arena. The arena was later moved to Filton. The walkway now connects the station’s new eastern entrance with the University of Bristol’s £500 million campus.

item.title: Smooth take off: Pilot handles Punjab turbulence; can he nail the landing for Cong?
item.description: Sachin Pilot has successfully brought together key leaders of the Punjab Congress, such as Channi and Warring, as they gear up for the 2027 assembly elections. With Rahul Gandhi positioned as the prominent figure of their campaign, this strategic move is designed to counter formidable opponents like the Aam Aadmi Party. However, Pilot now faces the crucial task of maintaining this unity through to the elections.

item.title: Poland joins coalition to strengthen Ukraine’s air defences against Russia
item.description: Poland has joined a significant anti-ballistic missile coalition with Ukraine and other European allies. This new project aims to develop an alternative and more affordable missile defense system. Prime Minister Donald Tusk also announced a substantial new donation package for Ukraine. The announcement occurred during the first Carpathian Summit focused on regional security and cooperation. Both nations emphasized their strong partnership and shared opposition to Russian aggression.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Mamata gets 'footballer', but can she win TMC 'khela'? Maharashtra shows a 'red card'
item.description: The Election Commission has designated new names and symbols for both Mamata Banerjee's faction and its competitor. This decision mirrors previous disputes seen in Maharashtra with Shiv Sena and NCP. The commission is now tasked with determining the rightful claim to the original TMC name and symbol, influenced heavily by recent Supreme Court decisions that prioritise organisational support in addition to electoral backing.

item.description: The Rs 22,569-crore IPO has become India’s second-largest public issue, behind Hyundai Motor India’s Rs 27,870-crore offering in 2024. It has also moved past LIC’s Rs 21,000-crore IPO of 2022, but remains smaller than Hyundai Motor India’s record issue.

item.description: The match was reduced to 20 overs per side after rain interrupted play at the Niranjan Shah Stadium. India posted 182 for six after being sent in to bat by Aussie skipper Jack Czosnek, with Chauhan making 54 off 34 balls and Anvay, son of former India captain Rahul Dravid, scoring 38 off 18.

item.title: India's metro boom: From one city to a network set to overtake the US
item.description: India's metro network has expanded significantly, now spanning 26 cities. The nation is nearing the US in metro network length, trailing only China. This rapid growth has occurred primarily within the last decade. Hundreds of kilometers of new metro lines are currently under construction. Future expansion will focus on integration and passenger demand for sustainability.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Tier-2 cities see housing prices rise nearly twice as fast as top 8 markets: Report
item.description: Residential prices in eleven emerging Tier-2 Indian cities have grown significantly faster. These smaller markets are now driving India's next phase of real estate expansion. Infrastructure development and rising consumption are supporting this accelerated price growth. Commercial activity is also expanding across these developing urban centers. Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities are projected to contribute substantially to India's real estate sector.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: ‘Fully compliant’: Nestlé India responds to FSSAI action over infant nutrition products
item.description: Nestlé India stated its infant nutrition products fully comply with regulations. The company submitted a detailed response to FSSAI regarding promotional claims. FSSAI initiated legal action over alleged non-compliances with infant nutrition product regulations. A separate sample of a Nestlé follow-up formula was found sub-standard. Three adjudication cases have been filed against Nestlé India for these products.
item.dc:creator: SIDDHI DHARMADHIKARI

item.title: Jantar Mantar attacker Swatantra Bhardwaj released from Tihar on 3-week interim bail
item.description: Swatantra Bhardwaj, the social media influencer, was released from Tihar Jail after a Delhi court granted him three weeks' interim bail related to an alleged assault charge. The court enforced strict rules, particularly preventing him from sharing details of the case online. Bhardwaj's detention earlier this month followed an incendiary interview. The next court date is set for October 6, where the situation will be reassessed.
